newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees 1996 GDP growth at six percent.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees 1996 GDP growth at six percent.

text.p: Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu on Wednesday reaffirmed the city state's estimate of 1996 gross domestic product (GDP) growth at six percent.
The Singapore government previously said its 1996 GDP growth would be "about six percent".
But Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong told Reuters in an interview on Saturday that figure might be "conservative".
Hu said Singapore's growth had slowed due to a cyclical downturn in the electronics sector worldwide.

"After three years of exceptional near 10 percent GDP growth which stretched into the first half of 1996, Singapore's growth slowed down abruptly in the third quarter this year to 3.2 percent because of a sharp fall-off in electronic exports," Hu told a local audience.
"Recovery is not expected until next year so that GDP growth as a whole has been revised downwards to six percent from an earlier forecast of 8.5 percent," he said.
Singapore is heavily dependent on electronics and related products, which account for about 50 percent of its industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
Hu said the present economic slowdown highlighted how vulnerable Singapore's economy was to fluctuations in worldwide demand.
